changes.location: Key Risk Themes › theme 1 (Long-standing Outlook and SharePoint hardening)
changes.before: Complete the long-standing Outlook and SharePoint hardening recommendations while preserving approved business integrations and confirming effective tenant settings.
changes.after: This theme covers the three recommendations first identified in 2024-Q2 that remain open: restricting additional storage providers in Outlook on the web, preventing user installation of Outlook add-ins, and requiring modern authentication for SharePoint applications. Irontrax should complete them while preserving approved business integrations and confirming effective tenant settings.
changes.reason: Converts an action-only bullet into a theme description that states what the theme covers before the recommended response.

changes.location: Key Risk Themes › theme 2 (Email and collaboration exposure)
changes.before: Close the email and collaboration gaps through attachment filtering, forwarding review, and proportionate external-sharing and meeting restrictions.
changes.after: This theme covers the routes through which information can leave Irontrax: forwarding, external storage, add-ins, and external sharing. Irontrax should close these gaps through attachment filtering, forwarding review, and proportionate external-sharing and meeting restrictions.
changes.reason: Explains the data-egress exposure the theme addresses before stating the response, linking the signals into one theme.

changes.location: Key Risk Themes › theme 3 (Data protection and mailbox logging)
changes.before: Establish effective data-protection coverage and verify mailbox logging. Score completion in a related control does not establish equivalent protection.
changes.after: This theme covers whether sensitive information is protected and whether mailbox activity can be reconstructed afterward. Irontrax should establish effective data-protection coverage and verify mailbox logging, because score completion in a related control does not establish equivalent protection.
changes.reason: States the scope of the theme and ties the recommendation to its rationale in one sentence.

changes.location: Key Risk Themes › theme 4 (Validation before assurance or procurement)
changes.before: Validate policy scope, licensing, and unassessed domains before drawing assurance conclusions or committing to additional products.
changes.after: This theme covers the licensing, policy-scope, and unassessed-domain questions that limit what the evidence supports. Irontrax should validate policy scope, licensing, and unassessed domains before drawing assurance conclusions or committing to additional products.
changes.reason: Names the evidence limits behind the theme before stating the response.

observations.location: Identity and Access › Identity control evidence table
observations.detail: The itemized control points sum to 58 earned (10 + 9 + 8 + 4 + 1 + 7 + 7 + 1 + 3 + 8) and 58 available, while the reported Identity score is 59/61. One earned point and two unearned points are not itemized in the table. The draft was not corrected.

observations.location: Data Protection and Collaboration › closing paragraph
observations.detail: The paragraph says the listed actions correspond to Active Recommendations 1 through 4, but the implement-active-DLP action does not appear in any of Active Recommendations 1 through 4. DLP appears only in the CIS recommendations table (2.1.2; 3.2.1). The Executive Summary also counts DLP among six newly emphasized controls.

observations.location: AI Agents and Generative AI Usage › closing paragraph
observations.detail: The paragraph says the awareness guidance in this report addresses verification of impersonation attempts. The Security Awareness call-out addresses cloud misconfigurations and shadow APIs. Impersonation verification is recorded as Q1 advisory guidance in Recommendation History. The paragraph was left unchanged.

observations.location: Data Protection and Collaboration › paragraph 1 vs Posture Summary
observations.detail: Paragraph 1 states that Irontrax holds Microsoft Business Standard and that the sensitivity-label action is unavailable. Posture Summary states that license flags are not independently verified entitlements, and no licensing evidence for Business Standard is cited. The phrase 'Business Premium or above Enterprise level licensing' is also ambiguous. Wording was preserved.

observations.location: Identity, Data Protection, Endpoint, Workload, and AI evidence tables
observations.detail: Evidence-status wording varies across tables: 'CIS not tested' (Identity), 'Exact CIS configuration not assessed' (Data Protection), and 'Not assessed' (Endpoint, Workload, AI). The draft does not establish whether these mean different things, so the wording was kept.

observations.location: Active Recommendations; CIS Microsoft 365 Foundation Benchmark; Recommendation History
observations.detail: Open items are described as 'To address' (Microsoft status), 'Open' (Action and Status columns), and 'open' (prose). Licensing is described as 'flagged licensed' in some places and 'Have license' Yes/No in others. Terms were kept as drafted.

observations.location: Active Recommendations and CIS Microsoft 365 Foundation Benchmark › Identified and Status columns
observations.detail: The template requires 'YYYY.QQ' in the Identified column and 'MM.DD.YYYY - <STATUS DESCRIPTION>' in the Status column. The draft supplies quarter labels such as '2024 Q2' and no per-item status dates, so the draft values were retained.

The draft Executive Summary omits the template's two standard introductory paragraphs, and the introductions to Key Risk Themes, Domain Posture, Security Signal Review, and Recommended Security Actions replace the template's standard wording with report-specific text. Key Risk Themes is a bulleted list where the template shows plain '<THEME>.  <DESCRIPTION>' paragraphs.

The template calls for a conclusion paragraph in this section and the draft had none. A closing paragraph was assembled only from conclusions already stated in the section (unassessed exposure; the cloud control baseline cannot be used to infer device status). No new fact was added.

The draft cites the Microsoft role names 'My Custom Apps', 'My Marketplace Apps', and 'My ReadWriteMailbox Apps'. The deterministic first-person scan flags the word 'My', so the role names were restated as 'custom apps, marketplace apps, and ReadWriteMailbox apps entries'. The original names and the same CIS reference (6.3.1) are in the draft.

The converted draft carried page-boundary markers, empty table header rows, and tables split across page breaks. These were normalized into single tables with a header row and separator. No cell content was changed by the normalization.
